R2.4.response: This was a real inconsistency and we are grateful it was caught. Classification and explanation are different operations with different costs, and the submitted paper used the two vocabularies interchangeably. The revision defines four terms once and then holds to them: a flow is any record the controller classifies, a positive prediction is a flow whose score reaches the threshold, an alert is a positive prediction dispatched to the operator, and a per-decision explanation is a TreeSHAP attribution computed for one specific alert. The explanation trigger is now a numbered equation rather than an implicit condition, and it includes the budget term that decides which alerts are attributed. Costs are reported against the quantity that drives them: classification cost per flow, explanation cost per generated explanation. The phrase "per DDoS flow" is gone, because the number of explanations is a policy variable and not a property of the traffic.
R2.4.action: Added Sec. III-B defining the four terms, added Eq. (2) defining the explanation trigger, rewrote Algorithm 1 so the trigger and budget are explicit, and swept the abstract, Sec. IV, Sec. VII and Sec. IX for consistent usage.
R2.4.location: Sec. III-B (Terminology), Eq. (2), Algorithm 1, Table 6 caption, and the abstract

R2.6.response: The reviewer is correct and the qualification matters more than we first appreciated. The bound rests on two different guarantees. The circular buffer gives worst-case constant-time admission and eviction. The hash map gives expected constant-time lookup, insertion and deletion, and degrades to linear in the number of distinct keys under adversarial collisions. The revision therefore claims expected amortized O(1) per admit/evict pair under stated data-structure assumptions, not unconditional O(1), and it notes the additional amortized cost contributed by periodic exact resynchronization when that mitigation is enabled. We also report the measured per-update cost in nanoseconds so the claim can be checked against a number rather than taken on trust.
R2.6.action: Rewrote the complexity claim in Sec. V-C with the assumptions named, and corrected the same claim in the abstract, Sec. II-A, Sec. IV and the Fig. 2 caption.
R2.6.location: Sec. V-C, abstract, Sec. II-A, Sec. IV, Fig. 2 caption

R2.9.response: We read the paper and found it genuinely relevant, though the application domain is distant. Chen et al. decompose an operational signal across time and frequency scales and transform each component into a Poincare plot, on the argument that scale-agnostic summary statistics discard exactly the information that separates a healthy machine from a degrading one. That is the same methodological move this paper makes with windowed entropy: replace a per-observation statistic with a distributional summary over a window, because the abnormality lives in the shape of the distribution. The parallel extends to the obligation it creates, which is to show that the summary tracks the condition of interest and not an incidental property of how the data were collected. We discuss the work on those terms and then answer that obligation for our own features with the shuffled-arrival-order experiment in Sec. VII.
R2.9.action: Added Sec. II-D on nonlinear dynamic indices for abnormal-state detection, discussing the work substantively and connecting it to our own validation requirement.

R4.3.response: Added as a dedicated discussion section covering each point raised. On deep learning in SDN, we report the accuracy, latency and explainability trade-off against measured numbers from our own CPU-only comparison rather than against published figures from different hardware, and we note two deployment caveats that accuracy tables hide: sequence models classify a window rather than a flow, so the unit of decision differs from the unit of enforcement, and graph models are transductive, so per-flow latency is not well defined without incremental graph maintenance. On SD-IoT, we work through latency and energy, reliability and scalability, heterogeneous traffic, and cross-layer coordination in turn. The cross-layer discussion is grounded in our TCAM measurements, which show the concrete failure mode: exact-match mitigation rules against a spoofed-source flood exhaust a bounded table and evict the entries carrying QoS policy, so the security function degrades service before the attack does. Prefix aggregation bounds occupancy by the number of attacking prefixes instead, which is what makes coordinated enforcement feasible. On lightweight and edge inference, we identify the serialized forest size as the binding constraint for a gateway deployment and point to the compression work that addresses it.
R4.3.action: Added Sec. IX-A (Deep learning for SDN DDoS detection, and the trade it offers) and Sec. IX-B (Adapting XAI-SDN to QoS-aware software-defined IoT), together with six supporting references.
R4.3.location: Sec. IX-B and Sec. IX-C; references [35]-[40]

R7.2.response: Following this up led us to a defect in our own pipeline, and we are glad the reviewer pressed on it. CICFlowMeter flow records contain no TTL field, and our feature extractor supplied a constant value of 64 for every flow. The TTL entropy feature was therefore identically zero across all 3,590,794 flows, with a standard deviation of 7.2e-18 and a single-feature AUC of 0.500021, which is chance. It contributed nothing to any result in the submitted paper. We have replaced it with source-port entropy, which is exported by CICFlowMeter, is non-degenerate, and is directly relevant to floods that randomize source ports. On the same measurements it reaches a single-feature AUC of 0.9876 and carries the highest mutual information of any entropy feature. The dimensionality of the representation is unchanged and all results have been recomputed. On binning, the revision now gives a table specifying, for each of the eight entropy features, the exact source field, the transformation and the bin width. We also state two things the earlier version left implicit: packet-length and inter-arrival entropy are computed over per-flow means rather than per-packet distributions, because the mean is what the exporter reports, and the flag entropy summarizes SYN counts rather than a full TCP flag bitmask.
R7.2.action: Replaced the defective feature, added the complete feature specification table, corrected Eq. (7), and recomputed every affected result.
R7.2.location: Sec. V-A, Table 3 (feature specification), Eq. (7); disclosed in Sec. VI-A
